import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set up the figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Specifications Analysis', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Color palette
palette = sns.color_palette("husl", n_colors=df['sensor_type'].nunique())

# Plot 1: Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
for i, sensor in enumerate(df['sensor_type'].unique()):
    subset = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax1.scatter(subset['megapixels'], subset['price_usd'], 
                alpha=0.6, label=sensor, s=30, c=[palette[i]])
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', fontsize=8, title_fontsize=9, loc='upper left')
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: Average Price by Brand (Top 10 brands by count)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
brand_counts = df['brand'].value_counts()
top_brands = brand_counts.head(10).index
df_top_brands = df[df['brand'].isin(top_brands)]
brand_avg_price = df_top_brands.groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=True)
colors = sns.color_palette("viridis", n_colors=len(brand_avg_price))
bars = ax2.barh(brand_avg_price.index, brand_avg_price.values, color=colors)
ax2.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Average Price by Top 10 Brands', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')
for bar, val in zip(bars, brand_avg_price.values):
    ax2.text(val + 50, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, f'${val:.0f}', 
             va='center', fontsize=9)

# Plot 3: Distribution of Megapixels by Body Type
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
body_types = df['body_type'].unique()
box_data = [df[df['body_type'] == bt]['megapixels'].dropna() for bt in body_types]
bp = ax3.boxplot(box_data, labels=body_types, patch_artist=True)
colors_box = sns.color_palette("Set2", n_colors=len(body_types))
for patch, color in zip(bp['boxes'], colors_box):
    patch.set_facecolor(color)
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax3.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Megapixel Distribution by Body Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Plot 4: 4K Video Capability Over Model Years
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
yearly_4k = df.groupby('model_year').agg({
    'has_video_4k': 'mean',
    'brand': 'count'
}).rename(columns={'brand': 'count', 'has_video_4k': 'pct_4k'})
yearly_4k['pct_4k'] = yearly_4k['pct_4k'] * 100

ax4_twin = ax4.twinx()
line1 = ax4.plot(yearly_4k.index, yearly_4k['pct_4k'], 'o-', color='#2ecc71', 
                  linewidth=2, markersize=6, label='% with 4K Video')
bars2 = ax4_twin.bar(yearly_4k.index, yearly_4k['count'], alpha=0.3, 
                      color='#3498db', label='Camera Count')
ax4.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Percentage with 4K Video (%)', fontsize=11, color='#2ecc71')
ax4_twin.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11, color='#3498db')
ax4.set_title('4K Video Adoption Over Time', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='#2ecc71')
ax4_twin.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor='#3498db')
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Combine legends
lines1, labels1 = ax4.get_legend_handles_labels()
lines2, labels2 = ax4_twin.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax4.legend(lines1 + lines2, labels1 + labels2, loc='upper left', fontsize=9)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
